claims.text: Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature preferentially disrupt protective oxide or passive films along eutectic phase boundaries.
Interphase regions are more corrosion-susceptible than the surrounding phases.
Exposure of interphase regions accelerates both mechanical wear and chemical corrosion through tribocorrosion synergy.
The target alloy has an interpenetrating microstructure of alternating phases with distinct corrosion resistances.
Rapid or directional solidification produces the stated interpenetrating eutectic microstructure.
Eutectic phase boundaries act as localized stress-concentration sites.
Eutectic phase boundaries are preferential sites for accelerated protective-film breakdown.
Sliding wear mechanically removes protective oxide or passive films preferentially at phase boundaries.
Removal of protective films exposes fresh reactive surfaces.
Fresh surface exposure promotes localized corrosion through micro-galvanic coupling between phases.
Thermally accelerated oxidation further weakens interphase interfaces.
The combined wear-corrosion effect produces degradation greater than the sum of isolated wear and corrosion effects.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will cause greater total mass loss and surface damage than either isolated wear or isolated corrosion.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will increase wear-scar depth or area relative to the isolated baseline cases.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will increase corrosion-pit density or size relative to the isolated baseline cases.
The proposed mechanism applies when microstructural heterogeneity occurs at a scale that makes phase-boundary effects relevant to surface degradation.

contradictions.description: The stated outcome only predicts degradation above either isolated baseline, whereas the mechanism and falsification rule require degradation beyond the arithmetic sum of isolated wear and corrosion. These are materially different synergy thresholds.
The design specifies that the corrosion-only set receives no mechanical loading but subsequently calls for identical mechanical loading across the sets.
